title: Debian Packages job fails - apt-get update cannot reach azure.archive.ubuntu.com (connection timed out)
signature: Could not connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com connection timed out|Network

failed_jobs.name: Debian Packages / Debian Packages
failed_jobs.symptom: apt-get install fails: cannot connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com:80 - connection timed out

key_errors: E: Failed to fetch http://azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/pool/main/b/build-essential/build-essential_12.10ubuntu1_amd64.deb  Could not connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com:80 (52.250.76.244), connection timed out
E: Unable to fetch some archives, maybe run apt-get update or try with --fix-missing?
root_cause: The Azure Ubuntu package mirror (azure.archive.ubuntu.com) was temporarily unreachable from the GitHub Actions runner. Multiple apt-get fetch attempts for packages including build-essential, python3-dev, python3-pip, and others all failed with connection timeout or connection refused errors. This is a transient network infrastructure issue unrelated to the PR change, which only touches src/bindings/python/src/pyopenvino/core/async_infer_queue.cpp.
recommended_actions: Re-queue the PR to trigger a new merge-queue run
Monitor if azure.archive.ubuntu.com recovers (same failure seen ~18 minutes earlier in run 32152602590)
Consider adding --fix-missing or retry logic to apt-get install steps
prevention_strategies: Add retry logic (apt-get install with --fix-missing or a loop) in CI workflows that install Debian packages. Consider caching installed packages or using alternative mirrors.
historical_context: Same failure seen in run 32152602590 (18 minutes earlier), affecting PR #37401. This is the second occurrence of this pattern today (2026-08-18).
